title: Chapter 13: A Comparison of Four Listed Companies; Zweig commentary

claims.text: Compare profitability, stability, growth, financial position, dividends and price on compatible definitions; business quality and the price demanded for it are distinct dimensions.
claims.anchor: vary much more widely than their operating performance

claims.text: A strong past growth rate beginning from a tiny base need not be sustainable at larger scale. Competition and industry arrangements must enter the forward appraisal.
A valuation preference does not forecast near-term relative performance. The source allows continued momentum in expensive shares and disappointment in apparently cheap ones.
claims.anchor: There was no reason to expect

claims.text: Separate acquired revenue from growth of existing operations, using consistent acquisition dates and comparable periods before treating headline expansion as organic growth.
A stock split changes the share count and unit price without itself increasing aggregate ownership value. Financing receipts likewise must not be mistaken for operating cash generation.
claims.anchor: doubles the number of its shares and halves their price

assimilation: Use a comparison matrix to expose the operating assumptions implicit in different multiples, then explain the selected preference without promising a time to convergence. Separate corporate actions and external financing from economic gains. Historical company cases remain source illustrations and never become prospective recommendations.
adversarial_review: Alphabetical adjacency is not randomized sampling. High-to-low historical price ranges assume impossible entry/exit knowledge and omit dividends and costs. A fine past record does not guarantee Emery access to cash. The 1999 comparison uses full-year results reported later, so it is hindsight-contaminated rather than an as-of decision dataset. Figure 13-1 reports EMC diluted EPS of $0.53 while prose says $0.92; preserve the definition conflict rather than mixing the figure with the 103-times multiple. Acquisition subtraction needs matched inclusion periods. The sequel includes a successful richly priced Expeditors outcome as well as failures, preventing a simplistic high-P/E-always-loses conclusion. Fixed statistical screens do not establish permanent protection.
memory_delta: Compare operating quality and price separately, normalize definitions and distinguish organic growth, financing and splits. A value preference requires a declared horizon and uncertainty; selected historical sequels cannot certify future performance.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 306-320 and inspected tables 13-1 and 13-2 and figure 13-1, including diluted earnings and subsequent-report timing.
